notes:
PIN. The pin reason on the rendered page is 'real page; stage A for quests rejects it as not_a_quest_page and the mission binder never reached it'. That is a routing failure, not a page problem: this is an ordinary {{Mission Header}} Zilart page with a two-bullet walkthrough, so it is read as an ordinary mission. Provenance and identity copied verbatim from the front matter; match_rule stays pinned_by_hand and match_conf stays medium, not upgraded.

TWO BULLETS, TWO STEPS, AND THEY ARE AN UNORDERED SET. The sub-bullet says outright 'These can be done in any order', so both steps share group 'awakening_cutscenes' and draw together. A strict ladder would mark Norg and then nothing at all until the player happened to walk past the Jeuno door in the right order.

THE REST OF THAT SUB-BULLET IS NOT A THIRD STEP. It continues '...but both must be completed before zoning to Ru'Lude Gardens to trigger Shadows of the Departed', and the header's Next field is Shadows of the Departed. The zoning is the NEXT mission's trigger, not a rung of this one, so it is not recorded -- doing so would put a marker in Ru'Lude Gardens for a mission that is already finished. Its own sub-sub-bullet ('the Quest will not trigger unless sufficient progress has been made in other questlines') is advice about that other mission and is likewise not a step here.

STEP 1 IS ONE RUNG WITH A FALLBACK, NOT TWO. Bullet 1 gives two ways to see the same cutscene: zone into Norg, or -- if it does not fire -- go to the Captain's Chamber and speak to Gilgamesh. One thing done two ways is one step. Gilgamesh carries it because he is the only entity the bullet names and the only thing in it that can hold a marker. The Captain's Chamber is a room inside Norg, not a named targetable entity, so it stays in the step note. The page gives no grid for either, so grid is null on both steps.

STEP 2 TARGETS THE DOOR, NOT ALDO. Bullet 2 says to click the door 'for another cutscene with Aldo' -- Aldo is who appears in the cutscene, not what you interact with, and marking him would send the player to the wrong side of the wall. The page writes the building as 'Neptune's Spire Inn'; I recorded the entity as 'Neptune's Spire', which is this page's own string with the descriptive 'Inn ... door' wording dropped, because that is the name this page actually contains. NAME AMBIGUITY, DISCLOSED: the shipped index carries both 'neptune's spire' and 'door:neptune's spire' as Lower Jeuno keys, so a 'Door:' form of this entity also exists somewhere in the game data. I did not write 'Door: Neptune's Spire' because this page never writes it and I have no in-game NPC dump to settle which of the two the click lands on (qmprobe's log has neither). If the marker fails in play, 'Door: Neptune's Spire' is the one other string worth trying.

START. The header's Start field is the literal word 'None', kept verbatim in start.raw. The mission is handed to you on completing Zilart Mission 16 and its first action is zoning into Norg, so there is no giver to quote. I recovered Gilgamesh in Norg from bullet 1 as the fallback start marker -- both names are on this page -- and flagged start_recovered_from_walkthrough and start_is_zone_entry so the recovery is visible. Norg is also the first-listed half of an unordered pair, so the start marker is a mild bias, not a claim about order.

GATES. Repeatable 'No' -> false. Expansion is the header's own words, 'Rise of the Zilart', copied rather than folded to the corpus's 'rotz' code. Previous is the wikilink [[Zilart Mission 16|The Celestial Nexus]]; the displayed title is recorded, with cat/area taken from this record's own identity and id left null. Level is empty and {{Mission Header}} has no Fame field at all, so gates.level is null and fame is null throughout -- 'the field does not exist', not 'zero'.

EVIDENCE. Nothing enters inventory anywhere in this mission: no items, no key items, no monsters, no rewards (Title and Reward both say None). Both steps are cutscenes, which no packet reports, so evidence is null on both. That is the expected answer, not a gap.

WIKITEXT NOISE. The walkthrough is wrapped in '{{#ifeq:{{{transcludesection|Instructions}}}|Instructions|' and closed by '}}'. That is transclusion plumbing rendered as visible text, not content, and nothing was read from it.

steps.note: the cutscene normally fires on zoning into Norg; if it does not, the bullet's own fallback is to go to the Captain's Chamber and speak to Gilgamesh there. One rung, two ways in, so the target is Gilgamesh -- the only entity named. The Captain's Chamber is a room inside Norg and is not a targetable entity; the page gives no grid for it. Unordered with step 2: the sub-bullet says these can be done in any order.

click the door the page calls the 'Neptune's Spire Inn' door, in Lower Jeuno; the reward is a cutscene with Aldo, who is not the target and is not standing there. Recorded under the page's own building name minus the descriptive wording -- see the name-ambiguity paragraph in notes. No grid on the page. Unordered with step 1.

notes:
NO HEADER, NO WALKTHROUGH, AND NO QUEST ON THE PAGE. Pinned as 'real page carrying no recognised header template', and the reason no template was recognised is that there is none: the cached wikitext (source_sha256 3ae80e8f...) is a logo image, an art thumbnail, one sentence dating the add-on scenario to September 2010, a blockquote of the old man's marketing blurb, a '==Related Links==' list (Vision of Abyssea, Heroes of Abyssea, the official PlayOnline page) and [[Category:Software]]. That is the whole page. The client tracks 'Scars of Abyssea' as quest/abyssea/175 because registering the add-on writes a quest row into the log; BG Wiki here documents the product, not that row.

NO GIVER, AND I DID NOT PROMOTE ONE. This is situation C. The page names no NPC anywhere -- not in the blurb, which refers only to an unnamed 'old man', and not in the links. So start.npc, start.zone and start.grid are all null, and start.raw is null too because there is no Start field to quote verbatim. The only proper nouns present are Abyssea itself and the two sibling add-on titles; none is a person, and none is a square a marker could sit on.

I DID NOT IMPORT A LADDER. Vision of Abyssea and Heroes of Abyssea are linked from this page, and Heroes of Abyssea is in this very batch -- both are the same kind of product page with no walkthrough, so there was nothing to borrow even if borrowing were allowed, and it is not. Nothing in the cache says how the in-game row is completed, and I will not guess at Cavernous Maws or a Vision of Abyssea NPC to fill the gap.

ONE STEP, AND IT IS A PLACEHOLDER. check_authored.py fails any record with an empty steps list, so the record carries a single rung that asserts as little as possible: kind other, target {type: none, name: null} so it can never place a marker and can never claim a hand-in, zone and grid null, source_bullets [0] because it comes from no walkthrough bullet -- there is no walkthrough to number. Confidence is low, which normally makes the emitter fall back to a start-NPC marker; there is no start NPC either, so this row draws nothing at all. For a page with no quest on it, drawing nothing is the correct outcome and the only honest one.

GATES ASSERT NOTHING. With no infobox there is no Fame, Previous, Level, Repeatable or Expansion field, so fame is null throughout, prev is [], level is null and jobs is []. repeatable and expansion are null and specifically NOT false/'abyssea': null here means 'the page says nothing about this', and a false in repeatable would tell the runtime to suppress a repeat marker on a claim this page never made. The add-on's release date and its position as the second Abyssea chapter are prose, not an Expansion field, so they stay in this note.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 1: Target is explicitly {none, null} rather than a bare null so the record cannot be read as an unknown target type, and so this rung can never draw a marker or be treated as a hand-in.
